kf: Lung cancer is the commonest cause of UK cancer death; skin signs may be the first clue.
**Paraneoplastic**: clubbing/HPOA, dermatomyositis, acanthosis/tripe palms, ectopic ACTH pigmentation.
**Local**: SVC obstruction (facial swelling, distended chest veins), Horner's syndrome; **direct**: skin metastases (chest wall, scalp).
Use smoking history as a red-flag multiplier; refer per NICE NG12. SVC obstruction is same-day.
myths: **"An acne-like rash on cancer treatment means stop the drug"**: EGFR rashes are managed with oncology protocols and often signal response.
patho_lead: Tumours affect skin through **growth factors, hormones, immunity and spread**.

mech.t: VEGF and PDGF (from platelet clumps bypassing the lung) drive clubbing and HPOA.
Small-cell tumours make ACTH: pigmentation, hypokalaemia.
Anti-tumour immunity cross-reacts with skin and muscle (dermatomyositis).
